description: This role deliberately does not extend the shared `patch-automerge` preset, because there is no patch-level bump of ReactFlux for it to automerge - there is nothing about ReactFlux for Renovate's custom manager to track at all.

ReactFlux publishes no versioned container images. The registry API for `electh/reactflux` returns 1159 tags: `latest`, one tag per commit named after the full 40-character git hash, and a `YYYY-MM-DD` series that stops at 2026-01-22. No version-shaped tag exists; `2026.08.22`, `v2026.08.22`, `2026.08.15`, `2026.06.22` and `release` were each requested individually and all answered 404. `reactflux_version` in defaults/main.yml is therefore the literal `latest` and carries no `# renovate:` annotation.

The absence is structural rather than an oversight upstream, which is why it is unlikely to fix itself. ReactFlux's `deploy-docker.yml` does ask docker/metadata-action for `type=match,pattern=v(.*),group=1` on tag pushes, so a `v2026.08.22` git tag is meant to become an image tag - but `scheduled-tag.yml` creates and pushes those tags with the repository's own GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub does not start workflow runs for pushes made with GITHUB_TOKEN. Every one of the last twenty runs of `deploy-docker.yml` has `head_branch: main`; not one was for a tag ref.

The image's OCI labels are no help either, and are an active trap: `org.opencontainers.image.version` reads `v2.11.4` and `org.opencontainers.image.title` reads `Caddy`, both inherited unchanged from the `caddy:2` base image the Dockerfile ends on. A version assertion written against that label would be asserting Caddy's version, not ReactFlux's.

What Renovate does track here - GitHub Actions, prek hooks, mise tools, the Molecule Python requirements and the Ansible roles and collections Molecule installs - is already automerged on a branch by the shared default preset, so the automation this role needs is in place without patch-automerge.

Should ReactFlux ever publish versioned images and this role pin one, revisit: ReactFlux is a compiled single-page application served by Caddy out of a document root inside the image, with no database, no volume and no state of any kind, so a patch bump carries none of the unattended-migration risk that keeps automerge off elsewhere in this fleet. The Molecule `default` scenario already runs the image the role names and reads the build stamp compiled into the served bundle back out of it, and `bin/compute-next-tag.sh` already follows a pinned version with no change. The evidence for automerging patch bumps would be there.
